citation: The Genealogical Index of the Newberry Library, Chicago. 4 vols. Boston: G. K. Hall & Co., 1960. A photostat edition of the Newberry Library's genealogical card index: family surname headings, each over a locality and the published genealogy, local history or periodical that treats the family there, with the Newberry call number.
author: The Newberry Library (compiler); G. K. Hall & Co. (publisher)
describes_date: the published genealogical literature to about 1959; the works it points at run from the seventeenth century to the 1950s
locator: Volume 1 (A-C) is Internet Archive file FL2091539_CP-130151_01.pdf, 987 pages, sha256 in chicago/4d/data/research/newberry_index/text/MANIFEST.json. Every record's locator names the volume, the index page and the lines of chicago/4d/data/research/newberry_index/text/vol_01_locality_cards.txt it was read from.
rights_note: Published 1960 by G. K. Hall & Co. and NOT cleared. The owner uploaded the four volumes to the Internet Archive in the opensource collection on 2026-09-03; that is where this project reads them, and it is not a rights determination. Nothing is derived from the volumes but text citations, which check_required allows; no image, no asset and no geometry may come from them.
access_notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-03 by fetching the Internet Archive metadata for chicago1835-newberry-genealogical-index and downloading volume 1 (202,857,468 bytes) in full. The item carries no derived djvu.txt — it was uploaded the same day and the derivation had not run — so the reading is made from the PDF's own text layer with pdftotext, which is what MANIFEST.json records. The text layer is POOR: the volumes are photostats of typed and hand-corrected cards, and 'Andreas' comes back as 'Andrest', 'Androcs', 'Anurcii' and 'A.:.!.;c,'. Forty cards were drawn at random and adjudicated by hand; 39 of 40 carry the locality the reading assigns them (data/research/newberry_index/precision_sample.json).
what_it_supplies: which published genealogies, county histories and periodicals treat a given family surname, and at which locality

for Chicago and Cook County specifically: 581 cards in volume 1 alone, pointing overwhelmingly at Andreas's History of Chicago, at Moses and Kirkland's History of Chicago (1895), at the 1839 Fergus directory and at Wood's 1881 volume
a ranked reading order — which unopened work carries the most surnames this project already holds
the Newberry call number, for anyone who can reach the shelf
what_it_does_not_supply: any forename. A card heads a FAMILY, not a person, and every identification it seems to offer is refused in the domain's crosswalk
any date, address, trade or household for anyone
any evidence that a family was in Chicago in 1835 — the locality on a card is the locality the cited BOOK treats, and the book may be about 1890
any statement of its own: it is an index, and everything it says is a pointer to somewhere else
note: A FINDING AID, and the project's gate treats it as one: tools/read_newberry_index.py --check FAILS if this source id ever appears in a resident, household, structure or reconstruction record. The whole failure mode of an index is that a surname in it looks like evidence.
